---
title: "Planned sensitivity checks"
subtitle: "Change one analysis choice at a time"
---

## Purpose

Run the predefined comparison and alternative analyses after the main metric
definitions and models have been fixed.

## Manuscript-prepared-data sensitivity

Every hypothesis receives a **manuscript-prepared-data sensitivity**. The same
new H01--H11 code and models are fitted twice: once to the newly prepared data
for the main analysis and once to the dataset prepared for the manuscript,
with only objectively demonstrable data errors corrected. This comparison
therefore isolates the effect of data preparation and metric calculation.

It does not rerun the manuscript's modelling implementation. Differences
between the full manuscript-generating analysis chain and the main analysis
are discussed in the audit with the author, but they are not treated as this
sensitivity analysis.

The permitted data corrections and required comparison fields are fixed in
[`manuscript_prepared_data_sensitivity.md`](../audit/decisions/manuscript_prepared_data_sensitivity.md).
Both scenarios report the same exact fitted-model sample sizes and 95%
confidence intervals.

## What this notebook uses and produces

- Uses: the main H01--H11 results, the H01--H11 results obtained from the
  manuscript-prepared dataset, the placement comparison, the decisions about
  which metrics remain interpretable, and a table listing every planned
  alternative analysis.
- Alternatives considered: 70%, 80%, and 90% coverage requirements; all
  near-eye records versus participant-days (one participant's record for one
  calendar day) measured at both positions; complementary chest results;
  omission of sparse sites or one site at a time; justified alternative
  outcome distributions or transformations; alternative ways to represent
  repeated measurements and time dependence; and approved alternatives for
  gaps or state definitions.
- Produces: the main-versus-manuscript-prepared-data comparison; sample counts
  for each additional alternative; and direct comparisons restricted to
  records shared by the main and alternative analyses. All comparisons report
  estimates with 95% confidence intervals; the exact participants,
  participant-days, time-resolved observations, and sites used by each model;
  model-fitting and distribution checks; influential-observation checks;
  warnings; and a conclusion about stability. Every comparison also reports
  the participants, participant-days or participant-level rows, one-hour or
  30-minute observations where applicable, and sites shared by both models.
- Fixed rules: change only one choice at a time; do not test every possible
  combination of alternatives; do not add temperature.

```{r}
#| label: setup-sensitivity-battery
#| eval: false

root <- normalizePath(
  Sys.getenv("QUARTO_PROJECT_DIR"),
  winslash = "/",
  mustWork = TRUE
)
source(file.path(root, "scripts/pipeline/paths_io.R"))
source(file.path(root, "scripts/pipeline/assertions.R"))

paths <- pipeline_paths(root)
```

Each conclusion will be classified as:

- **stable** when the conclusion and practical magnitude remain similar;
- **quantitatively sensitive** when the conclusion remains but the magnitude
  crosses a practical threshold defined before the comparison;
- **qualitatively sensitive** when the direction or statistical conclusion
  changes;
- **inconclusive** when the available information does not support a clear
  conclusion;
- **invalid** when the alternative analysis violates a required assumption; or
- **non-estimable** when the model cannot estimate the requested quantity.
